blurb: A fishing town turned into Asia's great treaty port.

facts.t: The writer Lu Xun spent his last ten years in Shanghai, in a terraced house on Shanyin Road, now a museum. He died in 1936; his tomb is in Lu Xun Park nearby.
The riverfront of banks and trading houses was built mostly between the 1900s and 1930s, when foreign concessions ran much of the city under their own laws after the Opium Wars.
